_comment: Declared, reasoned differences between packages/zip and Python's zipfile. Every entry must say WHY. Two things are never declarable: sourcesAgree:false (the package contradicting itself), and a crash.
_format: Keys are 'policy:stricter-than-python' (a blanket policy, see below), 'lenient:<basename>' (we accepted an archive Python refused -- the dangerous direction, declarable only per archive), or 'name:<ours>:<theirs>' (a name decoded differently).
policy:stricter-than-python: We refuse archives that Python's zipfile recovers from. Measured on the corpus, this covers three damage classes: an end-of-central-directory record whose declared comment length does not land at end of file; a central-directory offset pointing past the end; and an entry count larger than the directory actually holds. In each case the archive contradicts itself, and APPNOTE.TXT 6.3.10 specifies only how a WELL-FORMED archive is laid out -- it does not require a reader to reconstruct a broken one, so both readings are permitted and this is a policy choice rather than a defect. The choice is to refuse, for two reasons. First, this package is built to be pointed at untrusted input, and a reader that guesses what a self-inconsistent archive 'meant' is exactly how two readers end up disagreeing about what an archive contains -- the confusion that makes a scanner and an extractor see different files. Second, the strictness is only ever in the safe direction: the opposite case, where we accept something Python refuses, is NOT covered by this policy and fails the diff per archive, because that is the direction in which we might be the ones getting it wrong.
policy:version-needed-is-advisory: Python's zipfile refuses any archive whose central-directory 'version needed to extract' field exceeds 6.3 (NotImplementedError: 'zip file version N'). We ignore that field and validate the features the archive actually uses instead -- the compression method, the encryption flag, and whether ZIP64 records are present and well-formed -- refusing on those concretely. APPNOTE.TXT 6.3.10 §4.4.3 defines the field as the minimum version needed to extract, and it is advisory: it is set by the writer, is frequently wrong in archives found in the wild, and says nothing a reader cannot determine for itself by looking. Refusing on a claim rather than on a capability would reject archives this package can read perfectly well, while catching nothing it could not already catch. This exception is keyed on Python's exact message so it cannot quietly cover any other refusal; every other 'we accepted, Python refused' case still fails the diff.
